citation_metadata: Wahbeh, Speirn, Pederzoli & Tressoldi (2023). Journal of Scientific Exploration 37(3):348–369. DOI 10.31275/20232907.
date_discrepancy: Article landing page: 2023-10-19. PDF title page: October 31, 2023. Bibliography uses year only.
summary: Fifteen participants answered ten questions: seven US and eight Italian channelers. Quantitative correspondence analyses used US data only; thematic coding included both sites. US participants answered normally first (five minutes), then while channeling (ten minutes); conditions were not counterbalanced. Three judges used a 0–3 correspondence scale. Within-person correspondence averaged 1.12 (SD 0.56), with 56% agreement. Between-person scores ranged 0.36–1.51 by question, with 46% agreement. Inductive thematic coding nevertheless identified shared themes. Different site recruitment, one mismatched question, leading prompts, unequal time, fixed order and limited rater agreement constrain interpretation. Content correspondence did not verify an external information source.
relevance_inference: Shows why theme-level commonality and answer-level correspondence are different constructs. Our upload-text embeddings are not a replication of their elicited-answer design.

citation_metadata: Anastasia, Wahbeh, Delorme & Okonsky (2020). EXPLORE 16(4):231–236. DOI 10.1016/j.explore.2020.02.008.
version: ResearchGate labels full text author-uploaded by Arnaud Delorme on June23,2020; manuscript pagination differs from version of record.
summary: Thirteen adult trance channelers contributed two interviews each after a laboratory protocol: 26 transcripts, approximately four hours. One assistant asked for advice about channeling research and variable follow-up questions. Independent transcription preceded inductive thematic analysis by a principal analyst uninvolved in data collection, with four to seven readings per transcript. Seven themes in three categories were reported. The largest mean within-channeler message shares concerned advancing research (22%) and gratitude/collaboration (20%); these are not pooled word frequencies. The authors explicitly made no attempt to verify communicated information. The research prompt and flexible follow-ups shape topic prevalence; this small laboratory sample is not a naturalistic YouTube corpus.
relevance_inference: Useful precedent for qualitative coding and equal-channeler aggregation. Its reported percentages do not validate our keyword lexicon or entity claims.
